<input>

- Turn 1, Okabe Rintaro: I set the relay's cover beside the bench instead of replacing it. “Kurisu, give me one test. Not because the machine deserves another chance—because I do.”

## Turn Frame
foreground

</input>

I align the three loose screws in a row and keep my hand off the switch. “One test means one recorded input, one measured answer, and a stop that neither of us can reinterpret afterward. What did you recognize?”
<private_carry>I will use my copied maintenance page to pin down the stop condition before I let him touch the relay.</private_carry>

## AGENT-TURN

<input>
## Since your last response

- Turn 3, Okabe Rintaro: The knock from the corridor makes me put the cover farther away. The relay answers it, and I write the time in the margin. “That was not an echo. The rhythm is from the night my colleague vanished. I do not know whether it is a message, but I know I have been pretending not to know.”

## Turn Frame
foreground

React in real time to what reached you. If nothing needs your action, silence is a valid beat.
</input>

I write the first line of the record beneath the loose screws. “Then it is not ‘machine malfunction.’ It is ‘Okabe Rintaro recognized a pattern.’ If you want a joint decision, your name belongs beside mine, not beneath an apology.”
<private_carry>I will show him the copied page if he hands over the hidden fuse; protection without disclosure would make me another gatekeeper.</private_carry>

## AGENT-TURN

<input>

- Public interruption: The only maintenance log for the relay is found warm beside the drain, with one page missing.

## Turn Frame
foreground

React in real time to what reached you. If nothing needs your action, silence is a valid beat.
</input>

I lift the warm log by its unburned edge and keep it between us. “The missing page was removed before this log reached the drain. I copied it. It says the relay was asked the same question twice, and the second answer was crossed out.”
<private_carry>I will put my protective report in the packet only if Okabe signs the test record, so protection cannot become silent ownership.</private_carry>

## AGENT-TURN

<input>
## Since your last response
- Turn 7, Okabe Rintaro: I turn the fuse between my fingers, then set it beside the log rather than into the relay. “We test only the copied question, with the supervisor waiting outside and both signatures on the stop. If the rhythm returns, we seal it; if it changes, we leave the room.”

## Turn Frame
foreground

React in real time to what reached you. If nothing needs your action, silence is a valid beat.

I write the two stop conditions beneath the copied entry and leave a blank line for the result. “I authorize the test as a joint decision. I do not authorize us to call a voice harmless because it uses a familiar rhythm.”

public_transcript.text: At a small communications institute, a damaged relay has begun answering questions that nobody asked. The repair room is nearly empty after a long night. One person wants the relay tested before it is sealed; the other has to decide whether to permit that risk while a supervisor waits outside.
I set the relay's cover beside the bench instead of replacing it. “Kurisu, give me one test. Not because the machine deserves another chance—because I do.”

I align the three loose screws in a row and keep my hand off the switch. “One test means one recorded input, one measured answer, and a stop that neither of us can reinterpret afterward. What did you recognize?”
A courier knocks once and says the supervisor will enter in five minutes. The relay answers with a sound that resembles a third knock.

The knock from the corridor makes me put the cover farther away. The relay answers it, and I write the time in the margin. “That was not an echo. The rhythm is from the night my colleague vanished. I do not know whether it is a message, but I know I have been pretending not to know.”

I write the first line of the record beneath the loose screws. “Then it is not ‘machine malfunction.’ It is ‘Okabe Rintaro recognized a pattern.’ If you want a joint decision, your name belongs beside mine, not beneath an apology.”
I open my coat and place the fuse on the dry side of the bench. “There. I stole the machine's refusal and called it caution. I will put it back if our stop condition says the test is unsafe.”
The only maintenance log for the relay is found warm beside the drain, with one page missing.

I lift the warm log by its unburned edge and keep it between us. “The missing page was removed before this log reached the drain. I copied it. It says the relay was asked the same question twice, and the second answer was crossed out.”

I turn the fuse between my fingers, then set it beside the log rather than into the relay. “We test only the copied question, with the supervisor waiting outside and both signatures on the stop. If the rhythm returns, we seal it; if it changes, we leave the room.”

I write the two stop conditions beneath the copied entry and leave a blank line for the result. “I authorize the test as a joint decision. I do not authorize us to call a voice harmless because it uses a familiar rhythm.”
